reason: PLACO+ genome-wide across the frozen pair set requires ~180 core-hours on this machine
evidence: Measured on this hardware (Apple M-series, 8 cores, 8 GB RAM): placo.plus is per-SNP with numerical integration. Single-core 2,000 SNPs / 42.0 s = 48 SNP/s. Parallel over 7 cores 6,000 SNPs / 107.3 s = 56 SNP/s, i.e. parallelism gives ~1.2x not ~7x, so the bottleneck is not core count. insomnia x mdd merges to 1,129,775 shared SNPs => 337 min per pair genome-wide; 32 FDR-significant pairs => ~180 core-hours. Agent execution windows are ~10 min and detached jobs do not survive them.
alternatives_investigated: Parallelised with mclapply (measured, 1.2x). Considered vectorising placo.plus - not possible without reimplementing its numerical integration, which would no longer be the official method. Reduced-scan alternative implemented and declared instead.

reason: lambda_gc is not interpretable on a screened variant set
evidence: The insomnia x mdd screen reports lambda_gc = 23.18. This is an ARTEFACT OF SELECTION, not evidence of confounding: variants were pre-selected for P < 1e-5 in at least one trait, so the tested set is enriched for signal by construction and genomic control has no null to calibrate against. A genome-wide run would be required to produce an interpretable lambda. Recorded so the number is never reported as a QC failure or as evidence of inflation.
alternatives_investigated: Genome-wide run is the only fix; measured at 337 min/pair (see phase3.placo row).
